reason: FAQ quote states default encryption with AWS-owned KMS keys and the option to provide customer-managed KMS keys for identity data such as user and group attributes.
FAQ quote states data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
FAQ quote states that with an external IdP, Identity Center holds a synchronized copy of attributes and group membership but no passwords or MFA devices.
Table row under the instance comparison header reads Yes / No / No for management account, member account and standalone account.
Table row 'Delegated administrator can manage instance' reads Yes / No / No in the same column order as the claim.
Table row 'Multi-account permissions' reads Yes / No / No for management, member and standalone account instances.
Table row 'Replicating IAM Identity Center to additional Regions' reads Yes / No / No for management, member and standalone account instances.
Table row 'SAML 2.0 customer managed applications' reads Yes / No / No, so only the management account instance supports them.
Quotes state IAM Identity Center must be enabled in the same Region as the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory and the access portal uses the same access URL as the directory.
Quote advises assigning users directly and avoiding groups for management account access; the surrounding best-practice text gives the group-membership reason stated in the claim.
Quote states MFA settings can require MFA whenever users sign in from a new device or browser, or from an unknown IP address.

Quotes and their list context name FIDO2 authenticators (built-in and security keys), virtual authenticator apps and RADIUS MFA through AWS Managed Microsoft AD, all supported for browser console and AWS CLI v2.
Quote on the Identity Center directory users page: each user can register up to two virtual authenticator apps and six FIDO authenticators, a total of eight MFA devices.
Quote states MFA is turned on by default so all users must sign in with MFA plus user name and password; page scope is Identity Center directory users, matching the claim.
Quote states FIDO credentials are phishing-resistant because they are unique to the website where they were created, such as AWS.
FAQ quote states IAM Identity Center provisions new roles and you can attach the same policies used with existing IAM roles.
Quote states Multi-Region support is not available for Active Directory; context says a replicated instance must use an external IdP or the Identity Center directory.
FAQ quote states users can be granted multiple permission sets and, when accessing the account through the user portal, pick which one to assume for that session.
Quote states that when adding IAM Identity Center to an existing organization, all AWS Organizations features must be enabled.
Quotes state IAM Identity Center requires a two-way trust with the self-managed domain and one-way trusts do not work.
FAQ quote states IAM Identity Center is offered at no extra charge.
Quote states no outbound synchronization, so the external IdP is not updated with user and group changes made in IAM Identity Center.
FAQ quote names the two options: AD Connector or an AWS Managed Microsoft AD trust relationship.
Quote states only one AD Connector directory or one AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory at a time, and AWS Managed Microsoft AD for multiple domains or forests.
FAQ quote states only one directory or one SAML 2.0 IdP can be connected at a time, and the connected source can be changed.
Quote states the organization instance must be enabled in the management account and only one organization instance exists per management account.
Quote states one point of federation for multiple AWS managed applications and accounts: federate once, one certificate to manage with a SAML 2.0 IdP.
Quotes state access portal sign-in creates an authentication session and the user then reaches all assigned accounts, AWS managed and customer managed applications without additional sign ins.
Quote states the service is fully managed and operates across multiple Availability Zones to ensure availability during an AZ disruption.
Quotes state an opt-in Region must be enabled in all accounts whose access is managed and the action must be repeated for new accounts.

The quote supports all features and central control of account instance creation only 'as long as you haven't deployed' the instance in an opt-in Region; the claim sentence drops that condition (it sits only in qualifiers).
Quotes state an organization instance is enabled by signing in to the management account, and member-account administrative credentials enable an account instance.
Quotes state the organization instance is deployed in the management account, is the only instance that manages access to AWS accounts, and is recommended for all production use of applications.
Quotes state AWS Organizations is recommended but not required, and enabling with Organizations creates an organization instance.
Quotes state assignment creates Identity Center-controlled IAM roles in each account with the permission set's policies, and modifications update those policies and roles.
Quote states a permission set is a template you create and maintain that defines one or more IAM policies and simplifies assigning account access to users and groups.
Quote lists AWS managed, customer managed, inline and job-function policies, and an AWS managed or customer managed policy as permissions boundary.
Quotes state a 1 hour default, 1 hour minimum, 12 hour maximum, and created IAM roles have a maximum session duration of 12 hours.

Quotes support 'collection of permissions' applied to selected accounts automatically, modelled on job-function or any AWS managed policies; 'often' is not in the quote and the claim drops 'or any AWS managed policies'.
Both quotes state permission sets need, and are available only for, an organization instance of IAM Identity Center.
